title: 120 V 1500 W heater element on a base

sources.citation: The 120 V 1500 W resistance space-heater element, the usual top rating of NEC-region 120 V portable and small fixed heaters (makers' published ratings, typical figures, paraphrased, not one vendor's). Its resistance is V² / P = 14400 / 1500 = 9.6 Ω and its rated current P / V = 12.5 A. A nickel-chromium element's resistance rises only a few percent from cold to hot (a temperature coefficient of about 1e-4 per kelvin), so it is taken as constant at the rated (hot) value.
game-design: the element in a guard on a 400 × 120 mm base, 90 mm tall, with a terminal at each end; not modelled on a product.

game-design: the element's two terminals are pressure-plate screw clamps, marked for one copper conductor of 14 to 10 AWG, solid or stranded (two fit, and the second makes a worse termination, D8), not for aluminium; the plate grips 8 mm of a 10 ± 2 mm strip, so every in-tolerance strip seats fully. The marked torque, 1.8 N·m (about 16 lb·in), is chosen inside the 14 to 18 lb·in range makers give for wiring-device terminal screws (read for the 120 V lamp's holder); it is not a published heater figure. NFPA 70-2023 Art. 110.14(D) requires the marked value (cited by number); no UL 486A-B torque table is used. Not modelled on a product.
game-design: conductors reach each terminal from the base's end face and leave along ±x; not modelled on a product.
game-design: a slotted and Phillips combination head (common practice, not one product); the drive type is a name and its size is not modelled.

game-design: the screw-terminal class's R₀ applied to the heater's clamps. NBS Building Science Series 103 (W. J. Meese and R. W. Beausoliel, 1977; read in the P3 source pre-audit, ADR 0018 §4.1) measured good branch-circuit wiring-device screw terminals at 3 to 8 mV at 15 A, 0.2 to 0.5 mΩ; 0.3 mΩ is taken at the marked torque with a copper conductor at 20 °C. BSS 103 did not measure heater terminals.

game-design calibration (ADR 0018 §3.3, §11), the screw-terminal class's values: the heat path into the device, 0.026 W/K, is calibrated, not measured (with 14 AWG copper at 15 A it puts BSS 103's 18 to 36 W glowing connections between the Draper point, about 525 °C, and about 1000 °C). The clamp's heat capacity, 1.1 J/K, is a physics estimate: about 3 g of brass clamp parts × about 380 J/(kg·K). The heater's own heat at its terminals is not modelled.
